title: Palindrome Rearrangement Queries
code: """ URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/palindrome-rearrangement-queries/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr 2983. Palindrome Rearrangement Queries You are given a 0-indexed string s having an even length n. You are also given a 0-indexed 2D integer array, queries, where queries[i] = [a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i]. For each query i, you are allowed to perform the following operations: - Rearrange the characters within the substring s[a_i:b_i], where 0 <= a_i <= b_i < n/2. - Rearrange the characters within the substring s[c_i:d_i], where n/2 <= c_i <= d_i < n. For each query, your task is to determine whether it is possible to make s a palindrome by performing the operations. Each query is answered independently of the others. Return a 0-indexed array answer, where answer[i] == true if it is possible to make s a palindrome by performing operations specified by the i-th query, and false otherwise. Notes: - A substring is a contiguous sequence of characters within a string. - s[x:y] represents the substring consisting of characters from the index x to index y in s, both inclusive. Example 1: Input: s = "abcabc", queries = [[1,1,3,5],[0,2,5,5]] Output: [true,true] Explanation: In the first query: - a0 = 1, b0 = 1, c0 = 3, d0 = 5. - You are allowed to rearrange s[1:1] => acabc and s[3:5] => abcabc. - To make s a palindrome, s[3:5] can be rearranged to become => abccba. - Now, s is a palindrome. So, answer[0] = true. In the second query: - a1 = 0, b1 = 2, c1 = 5, d1 = 5. - You are allowed to rearrange s[0:2] => abcabc and s[5:5] => abcabc. - To make s a palindrome, s[0:2] can be rearranged to become => cbaabc. - Now, s is a palindrome. So, answer[1] = true. Example 2: Input: s = "abbcdecbba", queries = [[0,2,7,9]] Output: [false] Explanation: a0 = 0, b0 = 2, c0 = 7, d0 = 9. You are allowed to rearrange s[0:2] => abbcdecbba and s[7:9] => abbcdecbba. It is not possible to make s a palindrome by rearranging these substrings because s[3:6] is not a palindrome. So, answer[0] = false. Example 3: Input: s = "acbcab", queries = [[1,2,4,5]] Output: [true] Explanation: a0 = 1, b0 = 2, c0 = 4, d0 = 5. You are allowed to rearrange s[1:2] => acbcab and s[4:5] => acbcab. To make s a palindrome s[1:2] can be rearranged to become abccab. Then, s[4:5] can be rearranged to become abccba. Now, s is a palindrome. So, answer[0] = true. Constraints: 2 <= n == s.length <= 10^5 1 <= queries.length <= 10^5 queries[i].length == 4 a_i == queries[i][0], b_i == queries[i][1] c_i == queries[i][2], d_i == queries[i][3] 0 <= a_i <= b_i < n / 2 n / 2 <= c_i <= d_i < n n is even. s consists of only lowercase English letters. """ class Solution: def canMakePalindromeQueries(self, s: str, queries: List[List[int]]) -> List[bool]: pass sol = Solution() # Example 1 print( sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abcabc", [[1, 1, 3, 5], [0, 2, 5, 5]]) ) # [True, True] # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abcabc", [[1, 1, 3, 5], [0, 2, 5, 5]]) == [ # True, # True, # ] # # Example 2 # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abbcdecbba", [[0, 2, 7, 9]]) == [False] # # Example 3 # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("acbcab", [[1, 2, 4, 5]]) == [True] # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("aa", [[0, 0, 1, 1]]) == [True] # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("ab", [[0, 0, 1, 1]]) == [False] # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("zzzzzzzz", [[0, 3, 4, 7], [1, 1, 6, 6]]) == [ # True, # True, # ] # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abcxyz", [[1, 2, 3, 4]]) == [False] # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abccba", [[0, 2, 3, 5]]) == [True] # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abcd" * 25, [[0, 49, 50, 99]]) == [False] # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("aabaacaa", [[0, 1, 4, 4]]) == [False] # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("aaabbb", [[0, 1, 3, 3]]) == [False] # assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries( # "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" * 2, [[0, 25, 26, 51]] # ) == [True]
solution: """ URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/palindrome-rearrangement-queries/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr 2983. Palindrome Rearrangement Queries You are given a 0-indexed string s having an even length n. You are also given a 0-indexed 2D integer array, queries, where queries[i] = [a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i]. For each query i, you are allowed to perform the following operations: - Rearrange the characters within the substring s[a_i:b_i], where 0 <= a_i <= b_i < n/2. - Rearrange the characters within the substring s[c_i:d_i], where n/2 <= c_i <= d_i < n. For each query, your task is to determine whether it is possible to make s a palindrome by performing the operations. Each query is answered independently of the others. Return a 0-indexed array answer, where answer[i] == true if it is possible to make s a palindrome by performing operations specified by the i-th query, and false otherwise. Notes: - A substring is a contiguous sequence of characters within a string. - s[x:y] represents the substring consisting of characters from the index x to index y in s, both inclusive. Example 1: Input: s = "abcabc", queries = [[1,1,3,5],[0,2,5,5]] Output: [true,true] Explanation: In the first query: - a0 = 1, b0 = 1, c0 = 3, d0 = 5. - You are allowed to rearrange s[1:1] => acabc and s[3:5] => abcabc. - To make s a palindrome, s[3:5] can be rearranged to become => abccba. - Now, s is a palindrome. So, answer[0] = true. In the second query: - a1 = 0, b1 = 2, c1 = 5, d1 = 5. - You are allowed to rearrange s[0:2] => abcabc and s[5:5] => abcabc. - To make s a palindrome, s[0:2] can be rearranged to become => cbaabc. - Now, s is a palindrome. So, answer[1] = true. Example 2: Input: s = "abbcdecbba", queries = [[0,2,7,9]] Output: [false] Explanation: a0 = 0, b0 = 2, c0 = 7, d0 = 9. You are allowed to rearrange s[0:2] => abbcdecbba and s[7:9] => abbcdecbba. It is not possible to make s a palindrome by rearranging these substrings because s[3:6] is not a palindrome. So, answer[0] = false. Example 3: Input: s = "acbcab", queries = [[1,2,4,5]] Output: [true] Explanation: a0 = 1, b0 = 2, c0 = 4, d0 = 5. You are allowed to rearrange s[1:2] => acbcab and s[4:5] => acbcab. To make s a palindrome s[1:2] can be rearranged to become abccab. Then, s[4:5] can be rearranged to become abccba. Now, s is a palindrome. So, answer[0] = true. Constraints: 2 <= n == s.length <= 10^5 1 <= queries.length <= 10^5 queries[i].length == 4 a_i == queries[i][0], b_i == queries[i][1] c_i == queries[i][2], d_i == queries[i][3] 0 <= a_i <= b_i < n / 2 n / 2 <= c_i <= d_i < n n is even. s consists of only lowercase English letters. """ class Solution: def canMakePalindromeQueries(self, s: str, queries: List[List[int]]) -> List[bool]: n = len(s) m = n // 2 # number of pairs, pair indices 0..m-1 # A[p] = s[p] (left half), B[p] = s[n-1-p] (right half mirrored) A = s[:m] # Build B so that B[p] corresponds to the mirrored char for pair p B = "".join(s[n - 1 - p] for p in range(m)) # prefix counts for A and B: arrays of size 26 x (m+1) # We'll store as list of lists: prefA[ch][i] = count of ch in A[:i] prefA = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(26)] prefB = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(26)] for i in range(m): ai = ord(A[i]) - 97 bi = ord(B[i]) - 97 for c in range(26): prefA[c][i + 1] = prefA[c][i] prefB[c][i + 1] = prefB[c][i] prefA[ai][i + 1] += 1 prefB[bi][i + 1] += 1 # mismatch prefix: mis[i+1] = number of pairs among first i+1 with A[p]!=B[p] mis = [0] * (m + 1) for i in range(m): mis[i + 1] = mis[i] + (1 if A[i] != B[i] else 0) total_mis = mis[m] res: List[bool] = [] # helper to get count vector from pref arrays for interval [l..r] inclusive def get_counts(pref, l, r): # if l>r return zeros if l > r: return [0] * 26 out = [0] * 26 for c in range(26): out[c] = pref[c][r + 1] - pref[c][l] return out for a, b, c, d in queries: # convert right substring interval c..d into pair indices ql..qr in 0..m-1 ql = n - 1 - d qr = n - 1 - c # intersection of pair-index intervals il = max(a, ql) ir = min(b, qr) # 1) mismatches outside union must be zero mis_PL = mis[b + 1] - mis[a] mis_QR = mis[qr + 1] - mis[ql] mis_I = mis[ir + 1] - mis[il] if il <= ir else 0 mis_in_union = mis_PL + mis_QR - mis_I if total_mis - mis_in_union != 0: res.append(False) continue # compute counts L_counts = get_counts(prefA, a, b) # counts of left chars in P_L R_counts = get_counts(prefB, ql, qr) # counts of right chars in Q_R B_on_PL = get_counts(prefB, a, b) # B counts over indices in P_L A_on_QR = get_counts(prefA, ql, qr) # A counts over indices in Q_R B_on_I = get_counts(prefB, il, ir) if il <= ir else [0] * 26 A_on_I = get_counts(prefA, il, ir) if il <= ir else [0] * 26 # demands from one-sided pairs D_left_only = [B_on_PL[i] - B_on_I[i] for i in range(26)] D_right_only = [A_on_QR[i] - A_on_I[i] for i in range(26)] # remaining available after satisfying one-sided demands L_final = [L_counts[i] - D_left_only[i] for i in range(26)] R_final = [R_counts[i] - D_right_only[i] for i in range(26)] ok = True for i in range(26): if L_final[i] != R_final[i] or L_final[i] < 0 or R_final[i] < 0: ok = False break res.append(ok) return res sol = Solution() # Example 1 print( sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abcabc", [[1, 1, 3, 5], [0, 2, 5, 5]]) ) # [True, True] assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abcabc", [[1, 1, 3, 5], [0, 2, 5, 5]]) == [ True, True, ] # Example 2 assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abbcdecbba", [[0, 2, 7, 9]]) == [False] # Example 3 assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("acbcab", [[1, 2, 4, 5]]) == [True] assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("aa", [[0, 0, 1, 1]]) == [True] assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("ab", [[0, 0, 1, 1]]) == [False] assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("zzzzzzzz", [[0, 3, 4, 7], [1, 1, 6, 6]]) == [ True, True, ] assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abcxyz", [[1, 2, 3, 4]]) == [False] assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abccba", [[0, 2, 3, 5]]) == [True] assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("abcd" * 25, [[0, 49, 50, 99]]) == [False] assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("aabaacaa", [[0, 1, 4, 4]]) == [False] assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries("aaabbb", [[0, 1, 3, 3]]) == [False] assert sol.canMakePalindromeQueries( "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" * 2, [[0, 25, 26, 51]] ) == [True]
